Subject: Data residency / region pinning questions (Acme Bank)

Hi Rajesh / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the security and infra team. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment on the open items you raised around PII, retention, logging, and region pinning.

Recap of requirements you mentioned:
- Primary data residency in US (AWS us-east-1) for customer data and model inference.
- No customer data leaving the region for serving unless explicitly allowed.
- Cross-region failover plan for DR with encrypted backups only; need RTO/RPO targets.
- Audit logs and access logs retained for 12 months, with export capability.
- Proof points: SOC 2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration details, and architecture diagram for region pinning.

Our proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a short summary of how Redwood handles region pinning and failover (below).
2) Attach SOC 2 summary and a region-pinning diagram for your architecture review.
3) Suggest a technical deep-dive with Aditya (cc'd) to walk through async vs. sync replication and backup guarantees — can you share 30–60min availability next week?

Quick answers (high level):
- Region pinning: Redwood supports per-customer region pinning. You can opt for strict pinning (requests and storage confined to a single region) or an active-primary with a designated secondary region for failover.
- Cross-region failover: We provide an async failover configuration. By default we do not synchronously replicate KV caches or ephemeral session state across regions — persistent data (backups, logs) can be replicated to the secondary region with encryption in transit and at rest.
- Backups: Encrypted snapshots of persistent storage can be stored in the secondary region; retention/rotation policies are configurable.
- PII handling: We support redaction at ingestion and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for data-at-rest encryption.
- Logging & retention: Default audit/access log retention is 30 days; we can provision longer retention (12 months) as part of Dedicated/Private deployments.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary), region-pinning-diagram.png (high-level).

If that all matches your needs I'll coordinate the technical call.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success / Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the summary — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our side before we commit to the deep-dive:

1) When you say "strict pinning," does that guarantee that no replicas or telemetry (logs/metrics/traces) will be stored outside the pinned region? We need an explicit statement for our compliance review.
2) For the async failover: what are typical RPO / RTO numbers you observe? Are backups automatic, and can we restrict backup storage to only the secondary region (no third-region replication)?
3) Audit logs: you mentioned default 30 days — to meet our policy we need 12 months. Can that be configured via the console, or is this a Dedicated/Private-only capability?
4) PII handling: do you have any guidance on how you redact sensitive fields during inference (client-side tokenization vs server-side redaction)? Does Redwood offer SDKs or webhooks to scrub PII before it hits the platform?

Also please attach the SOC 2 evidence (summary is fine) and the diagram — we'll pass those to our compliance team.

-Rajesh

Hi Rajesh / Priya —

Thanks — great questions. I confirmed details with Aditya and Marissa; answers below at a level you can share with compliance. We can go deeper on the technical call.

1) Telemetry & replicas:
- Strict region pinning: we can configure an account so that all serving traffic, model execution, and persistent storage are confined to the specified region (e.g., us-east-1).
- Telemetry (metrics/traces): by default metrics are aggregated in Redwood’s control plane. For Private deployments we can restrict telemetry to your VPC. For Hosted/Dedicated, we can provide a compliance statement: no customer data is replicated to other regions for serving; aggregated metrics/health checks do not contain PII. We will provide explicit language for your Security Questionnaire.

2) Cross-region failover / backups:
- Failover mode is asynchronous. Typical observed RPO is on the order of minutes (configurable; depends on workload and batching). RTO depends on the size of the state and warmup time for serving nodes; for a typical config we estimate RTO in the ~5–20 minute range for warm standby in Dedicated setups.
- Backups: encrypted snapshots of persistent state (models optional, customer data) can be stored in the secondary region only — no automatic third-region replication unless configured.

3) Audit logs retention:
- 30-day default for Hosted; 12-month retention available for Dedicated and Private deployments. We can provision extended retention for Hosted with an add-on (storage + export). Exportable in compressed format to your storage (S3).

4) PII redaction & SDKs:
- We recommend client-side redaction for highest control. Server-side redaction is available as a processing pipeline: you can configure field-level redaction rules (PII patterns) at ingestion; we also provide SDK hooks so you can scrub or tokenize before sending.
- For customers that require no PII to be transmitted, we support a strict mode that rejects requests containing detected PII patterns (useful for regulated workloads).

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 type II summary) and region-pinning-diagram.png (high-level architecture).

Action items:
- Please confirm if you want strict region pinning (no cross-region replicas) vs. active-primary + secondary failover.
- If you approve a deep-dive, Aditya can run through the DR RTO/RPO tradeoffs and the configuration steps.

I’ll wait to hear your preference — happy to set the meeting.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Rajesh / Priya —

Happy to take the technical deep-dive. A few clarifications and what I'll cover in the call:

- Replication model: our control plane supports per-account region assignment. Persistent storage snapshots are asynchronously replicated to the designated secondary region; we do not perform automatic synchronous cross-region writes for low-latency serving. This is why RPO is typically "minutes" rather than zero.
- Failover flow: on primary region outage we promote the secondary region (manual or automated per your policy) and restore latest encrypted snapshot. Connectors to your KMS in the secondary region must be available; we recommend cross-region key policies if you plan for automated failover.
- Backups & retention: snapshots are retained per your configured policy; we can export to your S3 bucket in the region of your choice. No third-region replication unless explicitly configured.
- Logs & audit: access logs include request metadata (non-PII) by default; request payloads containing PII are redacted or omitted depending on ingest pipeline configuration.

Proposed times for a 45-minute technical session this week: Wed 2026-07-01 14:00-14:45 EDT or Thu 2026-07-02 11:00-11:45 EDT. Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
